claims.text: Parenteral bactericidal beta-lactams with an extremely broad spectrum.
claims.quote: Carbapenems are parenteral bactericidal beta-lactam antibiotics that have an extremely broad spectrum.

claims.text: Seizures and other CNS effects, mostly with CNS disorders, meningitis or renal impairment
claims.quote: Seizures and other adverse CNS experiences have been reported during treatment with Meropenem for injection. These experiences have occurred most commonly in patients with CNS disorders (e.g., brain lesions or history of seizures) or with bacterial meningitis and/or compromised renal function

claims.text: (imipenem not used in meningitis for seizure risk).
claims.quote: imipenem is not used in meningitis because it may cause seizures.
Clostridioides difficile- associated diarrhea (ranging from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis) has been reported.

claims.text: Hypersensitivity to carbapenems or prior anaphylaxis to beta-lactams.
claims.quote: Meropenem for injection is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any component of this product or to other drugs in the same class or in patients who have demonstrated anaphylactic reactions to beta (β)-lactams.

claims.text: Pregnancy: only when safer antibiotics aren't an option.
claims.quote: Carbapenems should only be used in pregnant patients when safer antibiotics are not an option.
claims.locator: Use of Carbapenems During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Lowers valproic acid levels: risk of breakthrough seizures.
claims.quote: Co-administration of meropenem for injection with valproic acid or divalproex sodium reduces the serum concentration of valproic acid potentially increasing the risk of breakthrough seizures.
